newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees to let South Africa join Lome.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees to let South Africa join Lome.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers agreed on Monday to let South Africa join the Lome Convention, opening Pretoria's way into the bloc's main trade arrangement with the developing world next month.

Agreement became possible after Spain agreed to lift its veto, having sought to link the issue to its search for better terms on fisheries as part of a broader trade package between the 15-nation bloc and South Africa.

"Of course in parallel further negotiations will be necessary on the free trade agreement and the wine and fisheries agreement with South Africa," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo told a news conference after EU ministers met.
Diplomats said the move followed EU ministers' recept of a letter from Pretoria pledging to continue negotiations on a broader trade package, prompting Spain to drop the linkeage.

Negotiations on the trade element of the package -- designed to give South Africa preferential treatment in its commercial dealings with the EU -- had bogged down, mainly over agricultural and wine exports.
Most EU countries viewed the Lome move as a way of encouraging the talks with Pretoria.
Madrid earlier blocked the idea of putting South Africa on a fast track to join the Convention because of concerns that it would slow a deal on fisheries in the trade deal.
A statement adopted at the meeting of EU foreign ministers stressed the linkeage between the two issues.
Membership of Lome -- expected at a meeting on April 24 -- will give South Africa access to preferential trade treatment and aid.
